label: First widget
title: Your first widget
description: Create a counter, preview your changes and import it into OverCrow.

blocks.html:
1. Download the kit

Install Node.js 22 or later, then download and extract the kit. Open a terminal in the extracted overcrow-creator-kit.

Download the creator kit ↓

Prefer to edit online? Use the Studio and download your project or package when ready.

2. Create a counter

blocks.title: Terminal · Windows or Linux
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Open the URL printed in the terminal and click +1. This browser preview reloads valid edits; an error leaves the last working version visible.

3. Make a change

Change colors in widget/styles.css or labels in widget/locales/en.mjs and widget/locales/fr.mjs. widget/index.html controls the layout.

To add two on each click, replace the existing increment() function in widget/view.js with:

Change the button label from +1 to +2 in widget/index.html.

4. Build a package

Stop the preview with Ctrl+C, then run:

blocks.title: From my-widget/
blocks.source:
npm run check
npm run package

blocks.html:
The terminal prints the .ocpkg path under .overcrow-output/. It contains the files in widget/.

5. Test in OverCrow

Import the package in Control Center, review its permissions and activate it from the overlay library. In a game, test clicks, resizing and hiding/showing the widget.

For an update, increase version in widget/manifest.json, then package and import again.

Next steps

Save preferences, call an API or try another example. The creator kit guide covers preview controls, native testing and PowerShell troubleshooting.

label: Installation
title: Installation
description: Get the creator kit, the SDK and OverCrow.

blocks.html:
Start with the kit

The creator kit includes the SDK, templates and local tools. Install Node.js 22+ and follow Your first widget.

Download the SDK

For an existing project, download overcrow.js, the TypeScript declarations and the MIT license. The example archives already include them.

Write JavaScript directly or compile TypeScript with your own tools. Ship the resulting static files; the .d.ts file supplies editor types.

System requirements

TaskLinuxWindows
Create, preview and packageNode.js 22+Node.js 22+
Run a package in the overlayImport in Control CenterImport in Control Center
Native development and devtoolsInstalled CLI and Control Center for the same userCompatible OverCrow installation
Native development displayOffscreen; import a package to test in gameSame behavior

Linux : Hyprland 0.55+ Wayland, Plasma 6 Wayland, GNOME 46–50 Wayland or X11/EWMH.
Windows : Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 x64, with WebView2 and the application’s graphics prerequisites.

Use windowed or borderless games. Exclusive fullscreen is unsupported.

Install OverCrow

Download an official release. On Linux, check that the native CLI is available:

If the command is missing, check the installed OverCrow package.

Import the SDK

Add this markup to your view’s index.html before loading the module:

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Load view.js with <script type="module" src="./view.js"></script>. Host services require OverCrow; the creator-kit browser preview simulates them.

Serve a plain HTML project

For a simple layout preview, serve the folder with your editor’s local server. With Python 3 installed, use:

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/. Double-clicking index.html can block JavaScript modules on file:// URLs. This static server provides no host services.

See available host services.

label: Concepts
title: How a widget works
description: An HTML view, a manifest and an optional controller.

blocks.html:
The view

A widget starts with a local HTML page. Write its interface with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. OverCrow provides the frame, position and panel opacity. Keep the HTML/body background transparent and check small sizes.

An optional controller

Add a second HTML document when requests or cached state should survive a native view reload. The view sends messages to this controller; the controller replies with data to display. Use storage for data that must survive a full restart.

Controller · data⇄runtime.send⇄View · interface

See a counter with a controller.

The manifest

The manifest identifies your widget, names its files and declares permissions. OverCrow checks these permissions for network requests, storage, clipboard writes and game events. Read the manifest guide.

From project to package

StepResult
DevelopEdit files and preview your widget.
PrepareValidate the manifest and calculate file hashes.
DistributeExport a .ocpkg, test it in OverCrow and follow marketplace admission.

Use a framework

Any framework that produces local static files can work. Run its build yourself and ship scripts, styles, images, fonts and licenses in the widget. WASM can handle local computation. Keep bundles small and pause unnecessary work when hidden.

The runtime blocks remote images, iframes, Web Workers and audio/video media. A network permission enables overcrow.fetch requests only. Use SDK data or an authorized HTTPS API; game memory and native modules are outside the widget’s access.

label: Creator kit
title: Creator kit
description: Create, preview and package a widget on Windows or Linux.

blocks.html:
Install Node.js 22+, then extract the kit. The source is available on GitHub; the download is pinned to this documentation revision.

Download the creator kit ↓   Or use the online Studio →

Create a project

blocks.title: From the extracted kit folder
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget --template counter --id com.example.my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Choose blank for an empty view, counter to start or checklist for saved tasks. Omit --id to generate an ID. Existing folders are protected. Full tutorial.

Project files

blocks.title: Only widget/ is packaged
blocks.source:
my-widget/
  widget/             # HTML, CSS, JS, manifest and SDK
  preview.json        # Simulated data
  tooling/            # Local tools
  package.json        # Development commands
  .overcrow-output/   # Exported packages

blocks.html:
Keep API keys, personal fixtures and build tools outside widget/. Place your framework’s compiled static output there.

Edit Counter/Checklist labels in widget/locales/en.mjs and fr.mjs. i18n.mjs updates data-i18n elements and the page language; edit interactions in view.js.

In Studio, select/reset templates in the header and manage files in the explorer. Update imports after renaming. Download the project to keep browser drafts elsewhere; the ZIP preserves empty folders.

Commands

CommandResult
npm run devBrowser preview; reloads valid edits.
npm run checkValidate sources and manifest without changes.
npm run packageCalculate hashes and export to .overcrow-output/.
npm run dev -- --nativeNative session; keeps the controller during view reloads.
npm run doctorReport Node, OS and native host availability.

Ctrl+C stops a session. For another preview port: npm run dev -- --port 4176.

Browser preview

Open the printed 127.0.0.1 URL. Simulate the session, language and overlay mode. Invalid edits keep the last valid view; permission changes require a restart.

  • The three-dot menu adjusts content scale (50–175%) and frame opacity (0–100%); starters use 100%. Use sliders or enter a percentage. Widget CSS backgrounds stay independent.
  • Drag the 22-pixel top strip to move. The starter’s lower-right handle resizes from its fixed upper-left corner. Arrow keys work when focused; Shift increases the step.
  • The eye controls passive visibility. Passive mode hides frame controls and updates SDK visibility and overlayMode. Close is illustrative. Escape or an outside click closes options.
  • Frame settings survive widget reloads until page refresh. OverCrow supplies this frame; keep it outside your widget.

Reload restarts view and controller. The simulator keeps widget data in temporary memory. SDK storage behavior.

Simulate data

Declare the matching HTTPS permission. Fixtures match exact method/URL, ignore request bodies and make no external request. Use text for text or status 503 for failure. Missing fixtures return fixture_missing. Named game events require replay.

Test the native engine

blocks.title: Windows and Linux
blocks.source:
npm run dev -- --native
npm run dev -- --native --devtools
npm run dev -- --native --replay ./events.json

blocks.html:
Linux requires Control Center and overcrow-widget; Windows requires a compatible installation. For a portable host, add --host "C:/Tools/OverCrow/OverCrow.exe".

The kit recalculates hashes and reloads valid views while retaining the controller. Restart after controller edits, expanded permissions or storage permission changes.

Offscreen session

Use devtools to inspect the native engine. Import a package to test overlay input, focus, capture and clipboard gestures.

Import your package

Import the printed path in Control Center, review permissions and activate the widget. Increase version in widget/manifest.json for each update. Hash suffixes preserve exports; they do not change the version.

Troubleshooting

If PowerShell blocks npm.ps1, use npm.cmd run dev or node tooling/overcrow.mjs dev.

JSON reports ok, error code, field and action; failure exits nonzero. OverCrow and the marketplace perform final validation. Look up an error.

Host services and widget examples.

label: Manifest
title: The manifest
description: Identify your widget and declare its files and permissions.

blocks.html:
Start with this manifest

This is enough for a local view. The kit generates file hashes when packaging.

Keep id stable across updates: it identifies the widget’s installation and storage.

Fields

FieldMeaning
schemaVersionThe number 1.
apiVersionThe string "1". Required for every widget.
idStable lowercase reverse-domain ID, such as com.example.my-widget.
versionWidget SemVer, such as 1.0.0; increase it for updates.
entrypoints.viewLocal HTML page to display.
entrypoints.controllerOptional local HTML controller.
permissionsThe network, events, storage, clipboard or native capabilities you need.
localizationLanguages you ship and the default locale.
presentationNative options and content sizing.
filesGenerated file sizes and SHA-256 hashes.

See API v1 host services and language declarations.

Allow an HTTPS request

This permission allows only GET /v2/items. Every route is exact, even with a trailing slash. Declare variable values with pathParams and URL parameters with queryParams. Network reference.

Include your files

Put HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, translations and licenses in widget/. Use relative ASCII paths, with no .., links or case collisions. Keep build tools outside this folder.

The generated files must match every packaged file; the manifest excludes its own hash. The native CLI requires this ledger for dev and package. Unknown fields are rejected.

Review added permissions and restart development to accept them. Preparation never infers permissions from your code.

Limits

ItemLimit
Package128 MiB; 4,096 entries including the manifest
Manifest1 MiB
Paths192 ASCII bytes

See the relevant API pages for request limits, messages and languages.

label: Network
title: Network requests
description: Read an HTTPS API with overcrow.fetch.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.fetch(url: string, options?: FetchOptions): Promise<OvercrowResponse>Send an allowed HTTPS request.
response.json(): Promise<unknown>Read the body once as JSON; validate its shape.
response.text(): Promise<string>Read the body once as text.
response.arrayBuffer(): Promise<ArrayBuffer>Read the body once as bytes.
FetchOptions accepts method?: string (GET by default; GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE) and body?: string | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | null. Other request options are unsupported.

Declare each HTTPS origin, method and exact route in the manifest. /api/ allows only that exact path, never its descendants. Network wildcards and prefixes are unsupported.

Variable IDs

A variable occupies one complete path segment. Declare its type and bound; here, /v2/orders/item/rhino_prime_set/top is allowed, but /v2/orders/item/rhino_prime_set/history is denied.

Declare each variable exactly once. Build the URL in JavaScript; the host validates the value on every request. See the method for reading the active game’s Steam ID.

  • integer: required min and max, from 0 to 9,007,199,254,740,991. Decimal digits only, without leading zeroes.
  • slug: ASCII letters, digits, _ and -; maxLength from 1 to 128.
  • enum: values lists 1–32 distinct unreserved ASCII strings (A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ ~ -), each 1–128 characters, except . and ...
  • string: query strings only; maxLength from 1 to 256 UTF-8 bytes, with no control characters.

Only integer, slug and enum are valid in pathParams. Every {name} must occupy one full segment, occur once and have one matching declaration; unused declarations are rejected. The path starts with / and contains fixed segments using only A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ ~ -, with no root-only path, percent encoding, . or .. segment, repeated slash, backslash, query or fragment. A final slash is significant.

URL parameters

Without queryParams, any query string is denied. Declare each allowed key with the same value types. Keys are optional unless required: true. This example allows ?page=2&sort=name, but rejects ?page=2&debug=true.

Use URLSearchParams to encode values. Repeated, unknown or encoded keys are denied, as are empty values and invalid encodings. Parameter names start with an ASCII letter followed by letters, digits or _, up to 32 characters.

Limits per widget: 32 routes. Per route: a 1,024-byte path, 8 path variables and 16 query keys. The complete URL must fit within 2,048 bytes.

An absent or empty queryParams also rejects a bare ?. Each pair needs = and a nonempty value. Values are decoded once (+ becomes a space); keys remain literal ASCII. All required keys must be present; their order does not matter. required is only valid for query parameters. Credentials and fragments, including a bare #, are rejected.

Read a JSON response

For this example, declare GET https://api.warframe.market/v2/items, with no parameters. Add this output to your view:

blocks.title: view.js · GET /v2/items

blocks.html:
Read the result

MemberBehavior
status / okHTTP status; ok is true for 200–299.
contentTypeContent type or null.
bodyUsedTrue after the first body read.
json()Parse the body once; validate the returned data before using it.
text() / arrayBuffer()Read text or bytes once. A second body read rejects with body_used.

A 404 or 503 is an HTTP response: check response.ok. A denied permission or timeout rejects the call with an SDK error.

Limits and permissions

The host limits requests to 30 seconds, 2 MiB for request bodies and 32 MiB for response bodies. It rejects redirects, proxies and local destinations. Bodies are sent as bytes; a string does not automatically set a JSON Content-Type.

headers, signal, cookies and ambient authentication are unsupported. A Promise.race can stop your wait, but does not cancel the native request. Ignore replies from superseded searches.

Use overcrow.fetch for external requests. This permission does not enable remote images, WebSockets, workers or iframes. Keep API keys out of distributed files; use a service you control for private credentials.

Handle failed loads

Keep the last valid data during refresh, distinguish empty results from errors, show cache age and offer a retry. Warframe Market in Studio shows this with a controller and cache. Look up error codes.

label: Game session
title: Game session
description: Read session state and follow its changes.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.game.snapshot(): Promise<GameSnapshot>Read the current game context once.
overcrow.game.onSnapshot(listener: (snapshot: GameSnapshot) => void): () => voidReceive future game snapshots; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.game.on(event: string, listener: (payload: CloneableJson) => void): () => voidListen for a declared named event; return an unsubscribe function.

Read once or follow changes

snapshot() takes a picture of the current state. Its Promise provides one result when you use await; it does not update your page afterward. Use this to read the Steam ID for a network request with a variable ID.

blocks.title: Read once

blocks.html:
No extra capability is required. Fields may be absent before a game session is available; an unknown Steam ID is not an error and a duration of zero is valid.

Follow changes

onSnapshot(callback) asks the SDK to call your function whenever a future game snapshot arrives. A callback is simply a function you pass for later. In snapshot => { ... }, the value before => is the function’s parameter and the braces contain the code to run with that value.

Subscribe first, then call snapshot() to initialize the display. Game subscriptions do not send an initial value; host service subscriptions do. The returned function, named stop below, removes the listener; call it when your component closes. This module creates its own output.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Snapshot fields

Field / typeMeaning
running?: booleanWhether the game is running.
selectedActive?: booleanWhether the selected game is active.
steamAppId?: number | nullSteam application ID for the active selected game; no user identity, title or artwork.
sessionElapsedMs?: number | nullCurrent session duration in milliseconds.
overlayMode?: 'passive' | 'interactive'Current overlay interaction mode.
fixture?: booleanTrue for fictional preview data.

The game snapshot contains session context only. CPU, memory, temperatures and FPS have separate permissions. Invalid snapshot types reject with invalid_response; malformed update events are ignored.

Named events

Declare event names in permissions.gameEvents, then pass a name and callback to game.on(event, listener). The host or your fixture must actually emit that name. Validate the event’s JSON payload against its own schema. This is separate from native game snapshots; a replay field named elapsedMs does not rename sessionElapsedMs.

Test with a fixture

Replay ordered events to test handlers without a game, then verify real session data in OverCrow.

label: Host services
title: OverCrow host services
description: Find telemetry, FPS, media and presentation services, their permissions and shared snapshot rules.

blocks.html:
Service index

Service / methodPermissionPurpose
overcrow.host.capabilities(): Promise<CapabilityMap>—Report support and granted access for each capability.
overcrow.telemetrytelemetry.readCPU, memory and host sensor temperatures.
overcrow.fpsfps.readFrame rate and freshness.
overcrow.mediamedia.read / media.controlTrack information / playback controls.
overcrow.assetsmedia.readRead artwork handles delivered to this widget.
overcrow.presentation—Native options and sizing; declare presentation in the manifest.

Services are added as OverCrow updates. This index describes the current SDK; keep apiVersion: "1" and handle unavailable or unsupported services. Each linked reference contains its complete method table and an example. Download the TypeScript definitions for all types.

Permissions and availability

Add only the needed capability names to permissions.capabilities in the manifest. The four names in the table are the complete capability list. OverCrow asks the user for consent; adding a permission requires new consent.

host.capabilities() returns each capability’s supported and granted booleans. Support does not imply consent or currently available data. Presentation uses its manifest declaration, with no capability name.

Read once or receive updates

snapshot() reads the state once. It returns a Promise: await waits for that single result. It does not keep your display up to date.

onSnapshot(callback) registers a function that the SDK calls with the current state, then with later changes. For telemetry, FPS, media and presentation, the first read is automatic. The game API differs: it sends future updates only.

A callback is simply your function, passed to the SDK to run later. In snapshot => { ... }, snapshot names the value received and the braces contain your code. This arrow syntax is a compact way to write a JavaScript function. The method returns another function: save it as stop and call stop() to unsubscribe when the view or component closes.

Snapshot results

StatusMeaning
readyCurrent data is present; a field can still be null.
staleOlder data, or null; show its age when available.
unavailableNo current source; data is null.
unsupportedThe host or platform has no provider; data is null.
permissionDeniedAccess was not granted; data is null.

Each ServiceSnapshot<T> contains status, data, an opaque contextId and a nonnegative, increasing revision; sampleAgeMs is optional. Keep missing measurements distinct from zero. Ignore asynchronous results when their context is no longer current.

A failed one-time read rejects with an SDK error. An initial subscription read failure delivers unavailable with data: null, contextId: null and revision: 0. Updates may be grouped; subscriptions are not an event history. The SDK allows up to 128 active service subscriptions and 32 pending service actions; the host may apply tighter limits.

Other SDK tools

See game context · widget storage · network · lifecycle and messages · languages · clipboard.

Built-in notes, stopwatch state, journal history and connected accounts are not exposed. Studio examples use fictional data; test actual providers and permissions in OverCrow.

label: Performance & FPS
title: Performance and FPS
description: Display available game measurements, with their units and freshness.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.telemetry.snapshot(): Promise<ServiceSnapshot<TelemetryData>>Read the current measurements once.
overcrow.telemetry.onSnapshot(listener: (snapshot: ServiceSnapshot<TelemetryData>) => void): () => voidReceive current and later measurements; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.fps.snapshot(): Promise<ServiceSnapshot<FpsData>>Read the current measurements once.
overcrow.fps.onSnapshot(listener: (snapshot: ServiceSnapshot<FpsData>) => void): () => voidReceive current and later measurements; return an unsubscribe function.

Build a compact performance display with telemetry for CPU, memory and temperatures, plus a separate FPS service. A missing measurement is not zero.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. Use telemetry.read for system measurements and fps.read for frame rate; omit either permission if unused. Declaring them requests user consent and does not guarantee platform support.

Display a live measurement

snapshot() reads once; use await to receive its result. onSnapshot(callback) receives the current state, then later updates. The callback is your function: in snapshot => { ... }, snapshot is the received value and the braces contain what runs for each update. The returned stop() function unsubscribes. Shared snapshot rules.

This module creates a CPU label. Put overcrow.js beside it and load it with <script type="module" src="./view.js"></script>.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Units and availability

FieldMeaning
normalizedCpuPercentHundredths0–10000; divide by 100 for total-machine CPU percent.
residentBytesBytes; divide by 1048576 for MiB.
cpuTemperatureMillicelsius, gpuTemperatureMillicelsiusHost sensor temperatures; divide by 1000 for °C.
FPS value, sampleAgeMs, staleFrame rate, measurement age in milliseconds, and freshness.

Every measurement can be null, even when the service is ready. Keep a stale label and its age when showing old data; an absent age is unknown. A service marked unsupported has no provider on that host.

Linux CPU and memory cover the selected Steam process group or manually selected process descendants. Windows uses the validated target process. Temperatures describe host sensors, not the game process. Windows CPU temperature is unavailable; Windows FPS needs the validated capture service. Native Wayland currently has no FPS source.

System measurements require telemetry.read; the game snapshot contains session context only. Browser preview measurements are fictional and FPS is unsupported by default.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Media
title: Media playback
description: Read native media information and use the controls offered by the current player.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.media.snapshot(): Promise<ServiceSnapshot<MediaData>>Read the current track once.
overcrow.media.onSnapshot(listener: (snapshot: ServiceSnapshot<MediaData>) => void): () => voidReceive current and later playback state; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.media.previous(): Promise<ActionResult>Queue the previous-track action.
overcrow.media.playPause(): Promise<ActionResult>Queue play or pause.
overcrow.media.next(): Promise<ActionResult>Queue the next-track action.
overcrow.assets.read(handle: string): Promise<Blob>Read a delivered artwork handle as a PNG Blob.

Show the track exposed by the native media service and let the user control playback. The available buttons depend on what the current player supports.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. media.read reads track information; media.control enables playback commands. For a display-only widget, remove the control permission. These sensitive permissions require an empty network list and clipboardWrite: false.

Display and control playback

snapshot() reads once; use await to receive its result. onSnapshot(callback) receives the current state, then later updates. The callback is your function: in snapshot => { ... }, snapshot is the received value and the braces contain what runs for each update. The returned stop() function unsubscribes. Shared snapshot rules.

This module creates a title and a button. Controls require a fresh snapshot and a click in an interactive view.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Track information and controls

Field / typeMeaning
title: string | nullTrack title.
artist: string | nullArtist name.
playbackState: 'playing' | 'paused' | 'stopped'Current playback state.
artworkHandle: string | nullOpaque handle for assets.read; never a URL.
actions: { previous: boolean; playPause: boolean; next: boolean }Actions supported by the current player; the control permission is still required.

Call playback actions directly from the click handler. The host checks the control permission and a short-lived, single-use user gesture. ActionResult is { status: "accepted" }: the command was queued. Follow the next media snapshot for the resulting state; catch failures such as permission_denied, unsupported_operation, stale_context or busy.

Artwork and storage

Only pass assets.read a handle supplied to this widget by the media service. The returned PNG is at most 512 KiB. Display it with URL.createObjectURL(blob) and revoke the URL when replaced or closed. Discard late reads if the track or context changed.

Either media permission requires an empty network list and clipboardWrite: false, and forces temporary storage even with storage: true. Native options remain host-owned. Studio media controls change fictional data only.

label: Options & sizing
title: Widget options and sizing
description: Declare native options and let users choose how the widget is sized.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.presentation.snapshot(): Promise<ServiceSnapshot<PresentationData>>Read current dimensions and native option values once.
overcrow.presentation.onSnapshot(listener: (snapshot: ServiceSnapshot<PresentationData>) => void): () => voidReceive current settings and later changes; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.presentation.reportSize(parameters: { readonly width: number; readonly height: number }): Promise<ActionResult>Report unscaled content size from a view; the host chooses the final frame size.

Declare native options

Merge this presentation object into your manifest. It adds a Show title checkbox to the native widget menu and declares support for fitting the content. No capability permission is needed; keep apiVersion: "1".

Apply native options

snapshot() reads once; await receives the result. onSnapshot(snapshot => { ... }) calls your function with the current settings and later changes. The returned stop() function unsubscribes. Shared snapshot rules.

This view shows or hides a title using the checkbox value. Keep the module beside overcrow.js.

blocks.title: view.js · native option

blocks.html:
Let users choose the size

presentation.sizing.fitToContent is required. It declares the fitting behavior your content supports. The user can always choose manual sizing; when fitting is supported, the native widget menu includes a Fit to content toggle.

fitToContentBehavior while fitting
"both"Content sets width and height. Frame resizing is disabled while fitting.
"height"The user resizes horizontally; content sets height.
falseManual sizing only; the fit toggle is hidden. Useful for content such as chat.

Optional defaultMode: "fit" | "manual" sets the initial choice. If omitted, fitting is the default when supported; otherwise manual sizing is used. fitToContent: false with defaultMode: "fit" is invalid. Turning fitting off lets the user resize both dimensions within the bounds. Widget code cannot change this choice.

preferred, min and max each require integer width and height from 1 to 4096, with min ≤ preferred ≤ max on each axis. preferred supplies the initial size and the fallback before measurement.

The separate view below reports unscaled CSS content dimensions. Measure content, not the viewport or a zoomed frame. The host applies user zoom once and clamps the result to the declared bounds and available overlay area. reportSize() is a hint: it never overrides manual geometry. Allow wrapping or scrolling when the content reaches a size limit.

blocks.title: view.js · content measurement

blocks.html:
Without a manifest presentation, the service reports unsupported. reportSize() requires a view and that declaration. Controllers reject with role_denied; dimensions outside 1–4096 reject with invalid_request. Success returns { status: "accepted" }. Report actual content changes; the host groups repeated reports.

Read settings and changes

PresentationData fieldMeaning
sizingMode: 'intrinsic' | 'autoHeight' | 'manual'Effective user choice: intrinsic for fitting both axes, autoHeight for fitting height, or manual when fitting is off.
width: number, height: numberCurrent viewport dimensions in unscaled CSS pixels.
options: Readonly<Record<string, boolean | number | string>>Native option values, keyed by their manifest IDs.

OverCrow supplies defaults and valid saved user choices. Option, sizing-mode and dimension changes arrive through presentation.onSnapshot. Check the status before reading snapshot.data. The SDK has no setter for native options or sizing mode, and no separate options-change event. Use widget storage for your own interface’s data.

Option types and limits

presentation.options is a flat list in the native menu. The schema has no groups or custom submenus; an enum opens its own list of choices.

TypeNative controlRequired fields
booleanCheckboxdefault: true / false.
enumDropdowndefault, choices: [{ value, label: { en, fr } }]. 2–16 unique choices; default must be one of them.
numberSliderdefault, min, max, step. Finite numbers within ±1,000,000; min < max, min ≤ default ≤ max and 0 < step ≤ max − min. Step controls the UI increment, not stored-value divisibility.

Declare at most 16 options. Each needs id, type, label: { en, fr } and default. IDs and enum values contain 1–48 ASCII characters, start with a lowercase letter and continue with letters, digits, _ or -; option IDs must be unique. Labels are plain text, 1–80 characters, with no surrounding whitespace or control characters. options may be omitted; sizing is required whenever presentation is declared.

Append either object below to presentation.options. Read the values from snapshot.data.options.itemLimit and snapshot.data.options.sortOrder. The browser preview uses a numeric field for number options.

label: Lifecycle
title: Lifecycle and messages
description: Keep state in a controller and react when the widget is hidden.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.runtime.role: 'controller' | 'view' | 'unavailable'Read-only role, fixed when the SDK loads.
overcrow.runtime.send(payload: CloneableJson): Promise<void>Send JSON to the other role in this widget.
overcrow.runtime.onMessage(listener: (payload: CloneableJson) => void): () => voidListen for future messages; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.lifecycle.onVisibility(listener: (visible: boolean) => void): () => voidFollow visibility changes; return an unsubscribe function.
overcrow.surface.invalidate(): Promise<void>Request a surface refresh.
View or controller

Add "controller": "controller.html" to entrypoints for an optional controller. Both documents import the SDK. A plain browser reports unavailable; native calls reject.

Share a counter

The controller owns the count. A new view sends hello to receive its current value.

Each listener is a callback: a function called later with the received value. In message => { ... }, message is its parameter. Store the returned unsubscribe function and call it when removing the component.

blocks.html:

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
send targets the other role. onMessage returns an unsubscribe function. To confirm that a message was processed, include a request ID and send a reply; the send promise alone confirms neither processing nor saving.

Messages must be plain JSON, at most 1 MiB and 64 levels deep. Functions, cycles, Date, Map, undefined and non-finite numbers are rejected.

Pause work when hidden

blocks.title: Visibility changes

blocks.html:
A hidden view may still have an active controller. Keep necessary state work running and pause unnecessary timers or animations.

Request a capture

await overcrow.surface.invalidate() asks OverCrow to refresh the surface. The runtime already observes page changes; reserve this call for a needed refresh rather than a continuous loop.

label: Storage
title: Widget storage
description: Read, write and remove local JSON data with overcrow.storage.

blocks.html:
Methods and signatures

Method / signaturePurpose
overcrow.storage.getInfo(): Promise<StorageInfo>Read the effective persistent or temporary policy.
overcrow.storage.get(key: string): Promise<CloneableJson | undefined>Read a JSON value; a missing key returns undefined.
overcrow.storage.set(key: string, value: CloneableJson): Promise<void>Save a JSON value; resolve after its transaction commits.
overcrow.storage.remove(key: string): Promise<void>Remove a key; a missing key also succeeds.

Keep data between sessions

Use overcrow.storage to save JSON locally. This API provides an isolated JSON store for each widget. It never reads or changes built-in notes, history, preferences or accounts. Native OverCrow uses IndexedDB. To request persistence, add this to permissions in your manifest:

Without this permission, or with sensitive media capabilities, storage is temporary. The Studio and browser preview always use temporary memory, cleared when the preview reloads or its simulated game session changes.

Save and read JSON

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html: get() returns undefined for a missing key; a saved null stays null. set() completes after its transaction commits. Check whether a successful write is temporary or persistent:

blocks.title: Storage mode
blocks.source:
const { mode } = await overcrow.storage.getInfo();
console.log(mode); // 'persistent' or 'temporary'

blocks.html:
Limits and errors

ItemLimit
Keys256 keys; 1–128 UTF-8 bytes each.
ValuesJSON only; 64 KiB per value, 64 nesting levels.
Operations32 pending requests; opening and each transaction time out after 5 seconds.

Catch errors around awaited calls. On storage_quota_exceeded or storage_unavailable, keep the displayed data and report the failure. invalid_storage_key and invalid_storage_value indicate invalid inputs. Other codes are busy, invalid_response, stale_context and bridge_unavailable.

Protect saved work

  • Keep the widget ID stable. Validate and version stored documents; preserve unreadable data for recovery.
  • A separate get() then set() is not atomic. Centralize concurrent writes in the controller.
  • Persistence is not a backup. SDK data is not included in exported packages or Studio project drafts.

Advanced IndexedDB use remains subject to the native policy; use a separate database, never overcrow.sdk.storage. Raw IndexedDB is unavailable in the online Studio. Never store credentials.

Declare your languages

Declare 1–16 unique locales, including the default, using forms such as fr, en or en-US. OverCrow uses an exact match for the Control Center preference, or your default otherwise.

Display translated text

Supply your own translations. getCurrent() reads once; onChanged(render) calls your render function on future changes. Subscribe before reading the initial locale, then unsubscribe when the view closes. This example creates its own output.

blocks.title: view.js · local dictionaries

blocks.html: Call stop() when removing the component. Without localization, getCurrent() returns null and no language-change event is emitted. You provide widget translations; marketplace listing translations are separate.

Show the result

Show “Copied” only after success. On refusal, let the user retry. Test gestures in OverCrow; browser previews cannot validate them. The SDK supports writing, with no clipboard read access.

label: Test
title: Test your widget
description: Inspect the native engine, replay events and test the game overlay.

blocks.html: Test with the creator kit

The kit validates sources, recalculates hashes and reloads the native view. The controller keeps running; restart after changing its code. Use this offscreen session for engine checks. Import a package to test the game overlay. For layout, use the kit and its reloading browser preview.

Use the Linux CLI

Build your framework if necessary, then prepare its static output and register that output with the native CLI. Permissions remain explicit; use a fresh private output directory for each preparation.

blocks.title: Linux · output parent must be private (0700)

blocks.html: Reload a prepared folder

The watcher groups edit bursts and accepts only consistent manifest and hashes. Invalid changes keep the last valid view and controller. Run your framework build yourself. Use npm run dev -- --native to recalculate hashes automatically.

Expanded permissions stop the session with capability_confirmation_required. Review the new manifest and start a fresh registration.

Load from a local server

blocks.title: Server must supply consistent manifest and files

blocks.html:
Use a numeric loopback address and explicit port; localhost is not accepted. The host downloads and freezes verified files. The widget does not connect directly to the server; this is not an HMR or WebSocket tunnel. --watch cannot be combined with --url.

Replay test events

Events follow file order, with non-decreasing timestamps. Limits are 1 MiB and 1,024 events. Replay runs again after a successful reload. Here elapsedMs is a fixture field, not the native snapshot's sessionElapsedMs.

Inspect errors

--devtools opens local developer tools. The terminal reports replacement failures; the inspector shows engine details. Console output can contain private data. Remove tokens and personal responses before sharing a report.

label: Distribute
title: Distribute a widget
description: Export a package and prepare its marketplace listing.

blocks.html:
Before export

  • Test small sizes, zoom, passive and interactive modes.
  • Handle loading, empty data, failure and recovery.
  • Check saving and returning after the view is hidden.
  • Include every local resource and license in the prepared bundle.

Build a package

Run npm run package in a Windows/Linux creator-kit project. The command prints the output path and recalculates hashes. See the complete flow. With the Linux native CLI:

The command validates manifest and files and creates a deterministic stored ZIP with the .ocpkg extension. It neither signs nor installs nor publishes. Changes to bytes require re-preparation, and each new published widget version needs a new version number.

Prepare a listing

listing.json describes the author, license, source and catalog translations. It is separate from runtime files. Listing translations do not declare languages actually supplied by the widget.

Read the marketplace creator guide ↗ and review policy ↗.

Marketplace screenshot. Add a PNG to your widget, for example widget/preview.png, before preparing its package. In the publication sidecar listing.json, set "preview": "preview.png" or another relative path such as "preview": "images/screenshot.png". The image must appear in the generated manifest.files ledger. Use a static PNG of at most 256 KiB and 1,024 × 1,024 pixels; 960 × 600 is a useful landscape format. URLs, SVGs, animated images and paths outside the widget are rejected.

The marketplace displays the admitted image on cards and detail pages, with a neutral placeholder if it is absent. Changing a published screenshot requires a new widget version and signed publication.

Review and installation

Review and publication use the validated listing, manifest and exact package bytes. The signed catalog and installation consent are separate from local development. “Open in OverCrow” opens a listing in Control Center; it does not install or activate a widget automatically.

Licenses

The SDK and examples here are MIT-licensed; keep their notices. They do not force you to license your own widget under MIT. The public policy for admitting third-party licenses is still pending; successful format validation alone does not authorize publication.

label: Troubleshooting
title: Troubleshooting
description: Find an error and the next step to try.

blocks.html:
Error codes

Symptom / codeLikely causeNext step
bridge_unavailableThe SDK cannot find the native runtime.Use dev or an installed package; a plain web server has no native bridge.
invalid_manifest / invalid_bundle / invalid widget projectSchema, path, file or hash is inconsistent.Check entrypoints and permissions, then prepare a fresh output.
unsafe_pathRelative path, symlink or incompatible permissions.Use a real absolute path and private 0700 output parent.
capability_confirmation_requiredReload requests more permissions.Review the change and explicitly restart development.
capability_denied / permission_deniedPermission or current user gesture is missing or expired.Check manifest and consent; click again in interactive mode for clipboard.
body_usedThe same response body was read twice.Read json(), text() or arrayBuffer() once and store the result.
invalid_message / message_too_largeMessage is not small, plain JSON.Avoid cycles and split large application data.
request_body_limitRequest body exceeds 2 MiB.Reduce the request or split it if the API permits.
busy / unresponsiveOperation overlaps or runtime did not respond in time.Disable duplicate actions, then offer a retry.
Blank view after an editJavaScript error, missing entrypoint or unprepared build.Open devtools, check index.html and prepare again.
Session events do not fireDeclaring a name does not create a live feed.Use onSnapshot for native updates; check replay event names/payloads.
HTTP 4xx / 5xxRemote service refused or failed.Check response.ok, show an error and retain last valid data.

Check three things

  1. Does the HTML render with local assets at the expected size?
  2. Is the widget running in OverCrow with required permissions?
  3. Does received data match the schema your code expects?

Report an issue

Include OverCrow, widget and SDK versions; platform; minimal steps; expected versus actual result; and error code. Use a small example or non-personal fixture. Application diagnostics can prepare a report for explicit submission.

Runtime limits

The SDK has no shell, Node, Tauri, arbitrary file access or game-memory reading. External browser network access is blocked. An invented manifest permission cannot open those boundaries.
